title: ChipBlocks signal types manifest
description: Signal-type registry. Per ADR-006 (Net / port / signal model) + ADR-007 (Active Variables). Block port signal types live here. Multi-domain from day one: DC voltage, DC current, digital, analog, optical, thermal, mechanical, ground. Adding a new signal type = adding one row. Connection compatibility rules are encoded via the `compatible_with` field.

id.description: Signal type id. Lowercase, kebab-case. Examples: 'dc-voltage', 'dc-current', 'digital', 'analog-voltage', 'optical', 'thermal', 'mechanical-force', 'ground'.

description.description: One-paragraph explanation of what this signal carries and when to use it.

category.description: Broad domain category. Used by the palette UI to group signal types and by the validator for compatibility heuristics.

units.description: SI unit string (e.g., 'V', 'A', 'W', 'K', 'N', 'lm'). Omit for signals without scalar units (digital, ground).

compatible_with.description: List of signal-type ids this signal can connect to without a warning. Same-type self-compatibility is implicit (a 'dc-voltage' always connects to a 'dc-voltage' cleanly). Listed entries are cross-type compatibilities flagged for user awareness — e.g., 'digital' is compatible_with 'gate-1' (carry-over from v1's ADR-001 gate-1 ↔ data-u1 special case).

notes.description: Optional notes — caveats, edge cases, future-direction comments.
